title: Malbec
description: Also called Côt or Auxerrois in France. Born in Cahors, reborn at altitude in Mendoza.
L: Explain its French origins and names

Malbec is a black grape with thick skins and deep colour, often inky purple with a magenta rim. It smells of plum, blackberry, black cherry and violet, sometimes with cocoa. Its tannins are usually ripe and soft, its acidity medium. It's one of the most recognisable reds by colour alone.

Malbec comes from south-west France, around Cahors, where it's also called Côt or Auxerrois. DNA shows its parents are Prunelard and Magdeleine Noire des Charentes, the latter also a parent of Merlot. Once widespread in Bordeaux, it suffered badly in the 1956 frost and from rot, and was largely replaced by Merlot.
Côt in Cahors; parents include a Merlot parent
Match each Malbec fact to its detail.
Malbec has deep French roots, though it's now most famous in Argentina.

Look for very deep purple colour, almost opaque, with a bright violet rim. On the nose, ripe plum and violet. On the palate, plush, soft tannins and ripe fruit, with medium acidity. Compared with Cabernet Sauvignon, Malbec feels rounder and less gripping, with less blackcurrant and more plum.
Which aroma is a classic sign of Malbec?
Violet, with plum, is Malbec's signature aroma.
Malbec is deep purple, with plum and violet
It comes from Cahors, where it's called Côt
It's rounder and softer than Cabernet Sauvignon
Explain why Argentina became its home
Name other countries that grow it

Malbec arrived in Argentina in 1853, brought by French agronomist Michel Aimé Pouget for Mendoza's new agricultural school. It thrived in the dry, sunny climate, free of the rot that troubled it in France. Today Argentina grows over 75% of the world's Malbec, about 45,000 hectares. April 17 is celebrated as World Malbec Day.

Mendoza is a high desert. Little rain means little rot. Strong sun ripens Malbec fully, giving soft tannins and ripe fruit. Cool nights at altitude keep acidity. Irrigation lets growers control water. In France's wetter climate, Malbec suffers from coulure, poor fruit set, which lowers yields.
Most of the world's Malbec is grown in France.
Not true. Argentina grows over 75% of it. France has a small area, mainly in Cahors.

Beyond Argentina and Cahors, Malbec grows in Chile, often blended; in Bordeaux, where it's a minor blending grape; in the Loire, as Côt; and in California, Washington and Australia. Argentina's Salta and Patagonia also make distinct styles: very intense at altitude in Salta, fresher in Patagonia's cool wind.
Pouget, a French agronomist, brought cuttings to Mendoza in 1853.
Argentina grows over 75% of the world's Malbec
Mendoza's dry, sunny climate keeps it healthy
It also grows in Cahors, Chile, Bordeaux and the US

Cahors, on the Lot river, must be at least 70% Malbec. Vineyards grow on river terraces and on the limestone plateau, the causse. The wines are dark, firm and often more tannic and savoury than Argentina's, with black fruit, earth and spice. In the Middle Ages they were called the black wine and shipped to London.
At least 70% Malbec, firm and savoury

Mendoza Malbec is riper and plusher, with plum, black cherry and violet, softer tannins and often oak. Altitude shapes the style: lower Luján de Cuyo gives rich, round wines; higher Valle de Uco gives fresher, more floral wines with firmer structure. Many producers now use less new oak than in the 2000s.
Ripe and plush; fresher at altitude
Match each description to its region.
The same grape gives a firmer style in France and a plusher one in Argentina.
Taste a Cahors next to a Mendoza Malbec. The colour will be similar, but the French one will feel more savoury and firm, the Argentine one riper and rounder.
Cahors must contain at least 70% Malbec.
Yes. Merlot and Tannat can make up the rest.
Cahors makes firm, savoury Malbec, once called the black wine
Altitude in the Valle de Uco brings freshness
Why high vineyards make dark wines
Explain how ultraviolet light affects skins

Air cools by about 0.6 degrees for every 100 m of altitude. Mendoza's vineyards lie from about 700 to 1,500 m; in Salta, some reach 3,000 m. Higher sites have cooler nights, so grapes keep acidity and aroma while still ripening in strong daytime sun.

At altitude, the atmosphere is thinner, and ultraviolet radiation is stronger, rising by roughly 10% for every 1,000 m. Grapes respond by producing more anthocyanins and tannins in their skins, as a natural sunscreen. Skins thicken. That's why high-altitude Malbec is so deeply coloured and structured.
Why does high-altitude Malbec have deeper colour?
Stronger UV light makes skins produce more pigment
Grapes protect themselves from UV by producing more anthocyanins, the pigments that colour wine.

The combination of strong light, cool nights and dry air gives Malbec its signature: dark colour, ripe fruit, fresh acidity and fine tannins. In the Valle de Uco, sites like Gualtallary and Paraje Altamira, at 1,100 to 1,500 m, now have their own geographical indications for this reason.
Which are effects of altitude on Malbec?
Mendoza is dry at every altitude; rain doesn't increase much with height there.
Altitude cools the air by about 0.6 degrees per 100 m
Stronger UV thickens skins and deepens colour
Cool nights keep acidity, giving dark yet fresh Malbec

In Argentina, Malbec is the partner of beef from the asado, from steak to chorizo. Its soft tannins and ripe fruit suit grilled meat, and its plushness handles chimichurri, a herb and garlic sauce. Cahors' firmer style suits duck, lamb and cassoulet. Mushroom dishes work well too.

Serve Malbec at 16 to 18 degrees. Most Argentine Malbec is made to drink within five years. Top examples from high sites, and good Cahors, can age 10 to 20 years, gaining leather, tobacco and dried fruit. Decanting helps young, structured examples.
Most within five years; the best for decades
What sauce is a classic partner for Malbec and steak in Argentina?
Chimichurri's herbs, garlic and vinegar suit Malbec's ripe fruit.

Malbec also makes rosé, often bright pink and fruity, good with empanadas. Some Argentine producers make lighter, fresher, unoaked Malbecs, served slightly cool. In Cahors, some wines are blended with Merlot for softness. The range is wider than the classic plush red.
Most Argentine Malbec is made to be drunk within a few years.
Yes. Most is fruity and approachable, though top examples age well.
Malbec suits beef, chimichurri, duck and lamb
Serve at 16 to 18 degrees; most is best within five years
Rosé and lighter, fresher Malbecs widen the range
Which aroma, with plum, is typical of Malbec?
Violet and plum are Malbec's signature.
High altitude gives Malbec paler colour.
Not true. Stronger UV makes skins thicker and darker.
Mendoza is dry, which keeps Malbec healthy.
Order these places from lowest to highest typical vineyard altitude.
Cahors is low; Salta has some of the world's highest vineyards.
Malbec is dark, plush and violet-scented
Cahors gives firm, savoury wines; Mendoza riper ones
It's a natural partner for grilled beef
